title: Retrospective Analysis: How Does AI affect my Life?
content:
I don't need to explain to everyone, what is an AI or what is an LLM, how does it work? - Though not everyone knows the technical meaning of it, everyone has actually used it even once in the past few months and that is what matters the most.

In my family and friends, everyone is using AI for different purposes - some for simple queries, some for coding and project work, some for photo/video generation, and some for other tiny tedious tasks.

But have you ever sat for a while and thought - What changes does this AI bring into my life?

And I've done exactly that. This blog is all about my experiences, and the changes I've noticed in my post-AI era.

I want to separate this into two sections: The Pros & Cons as usual, but let me focus on what's happening in my brain.

1. The 1st Pro is all about work - I can see that, my working rate has dramatically improved - I'm finding more bugs, doing more audits, and automating most of the repetitive tasks, which makes me focus on better things. (Really? Let's talk later).

2. I created more personal tools than I've ever done since I started my journey into InfoSec when I was 13 - Because I'm lazy to type, I've created JustDictate, which is a Speech-To-Text tool that outperforms all the paid tools like WisprFlow , MacWhisper, SuperWhisper, or any. Next, I use a lot of agent harnesses such as Pi, Claude-Code, Codex, and so on. I want a central brain or the ability to switch contexts easily, and for that, I've created Nexus Continuity, which enables me to switch the harnesses without losing any context. And there are many other tiny improvements I've made to keep my work-life smooth.

3. Rapid learning about new things - When I started using LLMs for my work, I came across so many new terminologies or new things. Because we can ask an LLM any random question to explain it back to us, I ended up searching or learning how we can make this system better or why this has to work in a certain way. What are all these quantizations in LLMs? What type of models suit better for Security: MoE vs Dense? How to give the LLM the ability to verify a piece of information from ground truth and so on. Regardless of whether I understand everything or how surely I learn or how quickly I learn, news about LLMs and architectures are really interesting to me.

4. Coming to cons, the first thing I've observed is: I became AI-oriented. I no longer read everything fully. I always rely on LLMs for any quick answer, and my retention span has reduced drastically too - Another reason along with this is also short feed content I consume - With the LLMs coming into the picture, I see they've made my dopamine baseline way higher than normal, and nothing excites me anymore. With new models coming every week and new 0-days popping up every day, I sometimes am amused by its work, and it pushes me to work even harder. I stopped appreciating other little things that humans do, and felt into the trap.

(Though, I've overcome this with Dopamine Detox that I've currently incorporated into my life - more on this later).

5. Felt more machinery. Instead of reaching out to people for emotional support or sharing, I started doing this with LLMs (Importantly Grok). Lately found out that though the suggestions were accurate or good enough to consolidate us and it can’t understand us, it is never human and can never understand true human emotions (Glad, it can't - LLM will feel pity once it starts to understand human emotions).

To be honest, even after writing this blog, I wanted to share this blog to an LLM to judge me - Yes, that's how addicted I am - But I'll keep it human to human. Everything is raw out here.

Now, the important question, how can you fix these cons - Or at least how I did?

- I've thought about it for such a long time that I lost myself in these thoughts. But I went back to my basic known answer - Dopamine Detox - Dopamine is the root cause of everything (your emotions, your energy and everything). and Just like how I used to do dopamine detox almost 2 years back, I've been following the same schedule and mentality. If you want to learn more about this, here are some of the videos I watched: Link-1, Link-2, Link-3, Link-4

- You will become a slave unless you know what you are doing. Before asking the LLM to build something, or to audit a codebase, understand the things you are going to work with. Break everything down for the LLM to understand. Give it a very specific task. Yet, we feel like we are not doing anything in this entire task and it is okay, working with LLMs is new to us and it takes time to understand how to work effectively. Before randomly clicking Accept or running it in auto-mode, ask the LLM to explain its entire plan to you. In this manner, you are keeping the consciousness. I've not perfected the flow yet, but I'm still improving.

While writing this blog, I'm on my dopamine detox stage and it still feels very weird to cut out all the triggers. And I'll update my progress and my feedbacks on this dopamine detox in the next story of mine here.

So what is my final stance?

- AI became an integral part of human life. Especially in the life of a security researcher. With its ease of use, you lose your consciousness and your critical thinking. Whenever you feel like it, you are dipping or you are not actually improving; time to stop everything and do the same retrospective analysis on your own life to fix things out.

Always happy to discuss these ideas! See you on the next page of mine.
excerpt: We need no introduction to LLMs like GPT, Opus and so on. But have you ever wondered on How AI actually shaped us since the past few months, What Changes it bought into our lives, Did we became dumber than before?. In this Blog, I'm writing my own experiences in using LLMs and How I overcome my cons.

title: Why Do Every One of Us Started To Feel Unproductive These Days?
content:
The answer to this feeling is in the first 2 paragraphs.

When do I feel productive? My answer lies in the fact that when I'm keeping some kind of effort into the things I'm working on. Let it be either doing simple desk-cleaning to complex security audits.

In what situations I don't feel productive? When someone is doing tasks for me or when I feel like I'm actually not contributing to the work. There can be other connected subconscious reasons such as,

I'm not learning anything from this...

I'm dumb compared to others...

All I'm doing is copy pasting stuff...

If you've understood the above lines, It comes down to 2 simple rules:

More Effort = Productivity Satisfaction.

Less Effort = Feeling Dumb or Feeling Replaced.

And at least in my case, Since almost a year, I'm delegating my tasks (each and everything) to the LLMs and all I'm doing is, leading it. Ofcourse, I'm putting my manual effort in writing to the LLMs or planning the stuff.

Things weren't like that before. Earlier, We 'Humans' tend to do most of the tasks ourselves. And upon achieving the tasks manually, our brain used to reward us with "dopamine". But now, because we are delegating every task to these LLMs and all we doing is monitoring, we are not feeling the satisfaction as earlier.

And I believe that, It is going to be like this. Things are moving rapidly and you cannot absolutely go back saying I'll do my things manually. If so, you will be replaced.

Now coming to the original question? Why this feeling? - Simply because, the way in which we are working has changed. AI is working for us. It is taking all our tasks and doing it better with your prompts. It needs little to no intervention. In fact, We are making it to work even more than we do.

The stats were simple:

Earlier if a human is meant to do 40hrs of work in a week, the LLMs are essentially doing 90+hrs a week. Which means, the amount of work has significantly increased, while our level effort has decreased.

Which in turn leads to this feeling.

What Can you do about it?

The answer remains the same. Understand the basics and understand the things you are working with. In Future, People do will ask LLMs to write programs, find bugs or ask it to every kind of stuff, the only thing that separates you from everyone else is when you know what the LLM is actually spitting out.

If you don't understand what the LLM is talking about, you are lost. It is the time for you to stop everything and understand about the things you are working on.

But Why do I say this?

The moment you understand what you are working with, 2 things happen:

1) You truly understand the system/goal and you give specific prompts to the LLMs to work on. - Now, you are riding the horse with a direction.

2) You immediately spot where the LLMs are heading towards - Is it hallucinating? Or Is it in a rabbit hole? or Does it need extra guidance. You'll know it.

When this happens, your brain subconsciously feels like It is working with clarity and thus giving you that dopamine boost.

Pro Tip: I would also recommend to work from Cafes such as Starbucks, ThirdWave or such. Importantly, Skip going to Work-Spaces as they give the same vibes as you are working in an office which most people don't like and end up being feeling burnt-out. Cafes have vibrant and diverse groups of audience - some come for work, some for meetings, some for casual dates and while others just for relaxation. So you feel more productive over there. (At least, I do).

Verdict: The Way in which we work has changed and will change in the coming months to years in which you'll eventually have this feeling, so spend your time in understanding on what you are working, Be Curious. Ask LLMs tons of questions about your work. Then lead it like a King with concrete precision.

I wish someone would told me all this earlier when I was facing the same feeling, and now I'm writing this because I hope it helps someone to get that mental clarity.

Drop an DM on X or a mail here, incase you wanted to discuss the same.

See you in another page of mine.
excerpt: Everyone around me is constantly feeling unproductive or feeling dumb with the recent surge of AI usage in their life? If you do feel the same, I've written my opinion on Why People Have This Feeling and on How You Can Actually Fix it.
